properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-18 for Mission Bay's second real-site pass: real, address-tagged OpenStreetMap building footprint for Radiance, a 99-unit, 9-story Bosa Development condominium tower at 325 China Basin St/330 Mission Bay Blvd N, completed circa 2008-2009, notable as one of the first major US condo developments to open after the 2008 financial crisis. Shares Assessor Block 8720 with its sister project Madrone. Point-in-polygon checked against DataSF's official redevelopment-area layer: this site falls in Mission Bay South, not Mission Bay North as this project's own brief informally grouped it. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: corrections to the description above: (1) the 99 units are supported by SFGate/Chronicle (March 22, 2009: 'the 99-unit Phase One of Radiance'), by the count of 99 per-unit condominium lots at 325 China Basin St and 330 Mission Bay Blvd N in the DataSF Assessor roll (year built 2008), and by SocketSite (March 2007: 'the 99 unit complex'); Bosa's page gives 693 units for Radiance, Madrone and Arden combined. (2) '9-story' is the taller of the two buildings per SFGate (a nine-story building and a six-story building); the OSM way cited says building:levels 8. (3) The OSM tag is name=, not addr:housename= (digitized_from fixed). 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint(s), not a hand trace or plan estimate. The underlying Assessor parcel is condo-mapped across many individually owned per-unit lots (confirmed against data/raw/parcels.geojson), so no single blklot represents the whole building and it cannot be joined via status.csv the way a single-owner parcel can. Using the real building footprint from OSM instead of a fabricated or arbitrarily chosen 'representative' unit lot, the same real-geometry-without-a-single-parcel pattern already used for several Pier 70 buildings (DataSF Building Footprints) and for Mission Bay's own real park polygons.'. REPLACED 2026-10-12 (shape; status and use unchanged): the owner approved building records whose outline matches an Assessor lot at 85% or better, both ways, using the lot (CLAUDE.md, 'An official parcel beats our drawing'). DataSF's Assessor layer (data/raw/parcels.geojson) has Assessor lot 8720018 (5,405 m2, active, mapped 2007-05-22); the earlier outline of 4,479 m2 and the lot overlap with IoU 0.83 (100% of the earlier outline lies inside the lot and it covers 83% of the lot). The outline is now that lot using the lots' own vertices (no simplification). The lot is condominium-mapped: 99 Assessor lots share this outline (the map lot 8720018 and 98 per-unit lots), so the outline is the building's shared lot, not any one unit. geometry_type stays 'real'. Previous accuracy_caveat: 'REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint(s), not a hand trace or plan estimate. The underlying Assessor parcel is condo-mapped across many individually owned per-unit lots (confirmed against DataSF's Assessor parcel data), so no single blklot represents the whole building and it cannot be matched to a single parcel record the way a single-owner parcel can. Using the real building footprint from OSM instead of a fabricated or arbitrarily chosen 'representative' unit lot, the same real-geometry-without-a-single-parcel pattern already used for several Pier 70 buildings (DataSF Building Footprints) and for Mission Bay's own real park polygons.'. 2026-10-12 audit corrections to the entries above (text only; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type): (1) Unit count: SFGate/Chronicle (March 22, 2009) says 'the 99-unit Phase One of Radiance' and 'The 99 units in the two buildings'; DBI permit 200505112126 reads 'erect a 9 stories 98 dwelling residential condos.' (proposed units 98). The 99 Assessor lot records that share this outline (the map lot 8720018 plus 98 per-unit lots) are a count of lots, not of homes, so they do not settle 98 against 99; the figure is about 99 (press) or 98 (permit). The SocketSite (March 2007) quote above has no URL in this record and was not re-read. (2) 'Completed circa 2008-2009' is not an event date: the Assessor gives 2008 as year built, the earliest dated press report is SFGate on March 22, 2009 (a sales report, published date), and DBI records permit 200505112126 complete on 2010-01-19 (permit 200806124266, 'renew pa# 2006/03/07/6167 for final inspection only', also completed 2010-01-19). No source read gives a move-in or opening date. (3) 'Shares Assessor Block 8720 with its sister project Madrone': the Radiance lots (325 China Basin St, 330 Mission Bay Blvd N) sit in block 8720 together with lots at 435 China Basin St and 420 and 480 Mission Bay Blvd in the Assessor layer, but no source read ties the name Madrone to those lots.
properties.accuracy_caveat: REAL lot geometry -- the outline is Assessor lot 8720018 (5,405 m2, active), so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a surveyed building footprint: it includes any yard, setback or plaza inside the lot and can sit a little off the walls. The lot is condominium-mapped: 99 Assessor lots share this outline (the map lot 8720018 and 98 per-unit lots), so the outline is the building's shared lot, not any one unit. Until 2026-10-12 this record showed the surveyed building footprint (OpenStreetMap (way 1258086102, name=Radiance at Mission Bay, 325 China Basin St)); 100% of that outline lies inside the lot and it covered 83% of the lot.
properties.notes: Story count: SFGate (March 22, 2009) describes Radiance Phase One as a nine-story building and a six-story building; the OSM way has building:levels 8. Bosa's page attributes the two connected 16-storey towers to Madrone, not Radiance.
